title: What to Pack in Your Gym Bag – NZ Essentials
meta_desc: Discover the ultimate packing list for New Zealand gym-goers. From must‑have basics to locker tips and chain‑specific perks, stay prepared and train smarter.
intro: A well‑packed gym bag saves time, keeps you motivated and ensures you have everything you need for a solid workout. Below is a practical, NZ‑focused guide that outlines what to bring, what most gyms already provide, and how to make the most of locker facilities.

sections.heading: Core items you should always pack
sections.body: These basics work for any gym, any workout, and any time of day. Keep them in a dedicated compartment so you can grab the bag and head out without a second thought. Even if your gym offers towels or water, having your own ensures hygiene and convenience.
list: Training shoes – breathable, appropriate for your chosen activity
Moisture‑wicking t‑shirt and shorts or leggings
Reusable water bottle (NZ tap water is safe and cheap)
Small towel – many gyms provide larger towels but a personal one is more hygienic
Deodorant and a travel‑size body wash
Lock for the locker (most NZ gyms use 4‑digit combination locks you set yourself)
Gym‑specific ID card or membership QR code

sections.heading: What most NZ gyms already provide
sections.body: Knowing what’s on‑site means you can lighten your bag and avoid unnecessary duplicates. Most chain gyms follow a similar standard, but always double‑check the facility’s website or call ahead.
list: Shower facilities with soap dispensers
Large towels for post‑shower use (often in the changing area)
Free drinking water stations throughout the floor
Lockers with built‑in combination locks (e.g., City Fitness, Anytime Fitness)
Basic first‑aid kits and defibrillators in the reception area

sections.heading: Chain‑specific extras to consider
sections.body: Different gym chains offer unique perks that can affect what you need to bring. Tailor your bag to the chain you train at to maximise comfort and cost‑effectiveness.
list: City Fitness – provides complimentary fresh fruit on weekdays; you may skip a snack pack.
Les Mills – offers on‑site yoga mats for group classes, so a personal mat is optional unless you prefer your own.
Jetts – 24/7 access means you might need a portable lock for off‑peak hours; consider a sturdy padlock.
Anytime Fitness – many locations have a free towel service for members; a small travel towel is still handy for sweaty sessions.

sections.heading: Locker room tips for a smooth session
sections.body: Lockers can be a bottleneck if you’re not organised. Follow these simple habits to keep the flow moving and protect your belongings.
list: Label your lock combination on a small card inside the locker – you’ll thank yourself if you forget.
Store a zip‑lock bag with spare socks and a spare shirt for unexpected showers.
Keep a small, waterproof pouch for electronics (phone, earbuds) to avoid water damage.
If you use the Exercise NZ subsidised gym scheme (40‑70% off), bring your eligibility card; some clubs require it for entry.

sections.heading: Quick checklist & next step
sections.body: Before you head out, run through this short checklist to ensure nothing’s missing. A well‑prepped bag means you can focus on your reps, not your rummaging.
list: Shoes, clothing, towel, water bottle, lock – all in the main compartment
Personal hygiene items in a zip‑lock bag
Gym ID/QR code and Exercise NZ eligibility card (if applicable)
Optional extras: snack, personal yoga mat, earbuds
